latest_release.name: v1.19.0 - Trace Your Workflows, Layer by Layer
latest_release.body:
**Dify 1.19.0 brings nested workflow tracing to your observability tools.** Follow a workflow into the Workflow Tools it calls, inspect the steps inside each invocation, and keep the LLM context alongside the execution tree. This release also makes Workflow Tools portable with App packages, adds Skill Hub automation, and makes Agent files easier to upload and preview. The bundled plugin daemon is upgraded to **0.6.14-local**. [Release highlights](#user-content-release-highlights) · [Upgrade guide](#user-content-upgrade-guide) · [Detailed changes](#user-content-detailed-changes) ## Release highlights ### Nested workflow tracing **See what happens inside a Workflow Tool, all the way down to its LLM calls.** Building on the Console drilldown introduced in 1.18.0, new external traces now include the persisted execution steps inside called Workflow Tools. Child steps appear beneath the Tool span that invoked them, preserving the hierarchy across nested and repeated calls. (#44673) ![Langfuse trace tree showing a workflow, nested Middle and Child Workflow Tools, and the selected LLM call with formatted prompts and responses](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/langgenius/dify/dcfb52e62726c91b43db20f3c087acf285428df1/docs/assets/pr-44673-langfuse-nested-prompts.jpg) *From the outer workflow to a nested LLM call: the execution tree and formatted messages, together in Langfuse. Screenshot from [#44673](https://github.com/langgenius/dify/pull/44673).* - **Follow the hierarchy.** Expand called Workflow Tools to see their internal execution steps under the invoking Tool span. - **Understand each invocation.** Repeated calls and failures retain their place in the trace. - **Keep the LLM context.** Inspect formatted prompts and responses, token usage, and project, trace, and observation links. > [!NOTE] > **Your saved provider settings continue to work.** The richer hierarchy applies to new executions; historical traces are not backfilled. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. For rolling deployments, follow the [tracing queue transition](#user-content-upgrade-guide) below. ### Take Workflow Tools with your apps Export an app and bring the workflows behind its Workflow Tools with it. `.ifpkg` packages include those workflows at their bound versions, including transitive dependencies. Import reuses tools already in the destination workspace and recreates, publishes, and registers missing ones, remapping their references. (#44592) All Dify app exports now use **package format v2**, including apps without Workflow Tools. Existing v1 imports and explicit YAML export remain supported. See the [upgrade guide](#user-content-upgrade-guide) before importing new packages into older installations. (#45353) ### Upload together. Preview in place. Select or drop multiple Agent configuration files and upload them in parallel. Successful uploads are bound in one atomic batch, concurrent Composer saves preserve the latest files, and Prompt uploads keep the cursor position while inserting multiple references. (#44947) Read PDFs inline, inspect source files with syntax highlighting, and see when text has been truncated. Previews cover configured files, Skill members, and working-directory files, with a download action when a PDF cannot be loaded. (#45032, #45045)
See Agent file uploads and previews ![Inline PDF preview in Agent files, with the research brief and file list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22bafc75-c8f5-46fd-b7ba-c5097f9cffb6) *Read a PDF directly in the Agent file preview and switch between project files.* ![Agent batch upload dialog with a PDF, Python source file, and Markdown guidelines selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5eafd0c1-f46d-4966-bbc0-e6cd5eacff02) *Select several files and upload them together.* ![Syntax-hi
